Renamed from inherited-releases.json on 2026-08-30. The old name stopped
covering the file's job the moment this repository published one of its own:
the release floor is derived from everything here, and a version published
HERE bounds the floor exactly as an inherited one does. Keeping the old name
and adding a non-inherited row would have made the filename a lie.
`pinnable = false` means the version exists permanently and must never be
depended on. That is not the same as absent, and the distinction is the whole
reason this file lists it: an index cannot un-publish, so the only place a
'do not pin this' fact can live is here and in the guard that reads it.

releases.release_run_note: Not recorded in the dossier at extraction time. Absent rather than guessed: a run id invented to fill the field would be a coordinate that resolves to nothing.

Tagged only after the wheel was installed back from the private index and conformance-checked. a2 rather than a1 is the first admissible composition version: a1 published the stable-verdict contract but did not recover the losing first-arrival transaction after the receipt unique constraint selected a winner.

releases.tag_note: NOT TAGGED, and must not be. A tag is this repository's assertion that a release was verified; a3's verification returned UNPROVABLE.
releases.release_run_note: Published by a run cancelled during its own verify job: the upload succeeded, the read-back, consumer proof and tag never ran. Verify run 33296262948 returned UNPROVABLE on property 1 — the sdist was never retrieved or compared by any automated check. Both artifacts were LATER confirmed byte-correct out of band (wheel 45,911 bytes, sdist 42,256 bytes, both sha256-matching the release run's build), so the BYTES are sound and the EVIDENCE CHAIN is not. Michael ruled 2026-08-30: immutable, unprovable, never pinnable, superseded by a4.

Published by run 33297423568 from the exact tip of protected main. Its tag was written in that same run by a job that called itself a verification and could not perform one: it compared hashes over whatever `pip download` returned (the wheel; never the sdist) and swallowed the install result with `|| true`. INDEPENDENT verify run 33310594187 later returned VERIFIED against the registry — both artifacts fetched by name and sha256-equal to the release run's build, provenance closed on peeled commit 2c61540f74018b7e19d7c5add893e0653cfcdb17, publisher read-back, read-only consumer install, and exactly one wheel and one sdist on the index. Michael ruled 2026-08-30: published and independently provable, so a4 is retained and never republished. The tag is left exactly where that run wrote it and is never moved.
releases.unpinnable_reason: SUPERSEDED BY 0.1.0a5 FOR FUNCTIONAL REASONS, NOT IDENTITY ONES. a4's five identity proofs stand and are recorded above unchanged. It is refused here because it cannot be adopted: `approve_plan` refuses a correctly-supplied approval digest with "the plan changed after approval" whenever the caller uses the other encoding of the same digest (`propose_plan` stored bare hex, `spec_digest` produced the `sha256:`-prefixed form, and the comparison was between two strings), and the published wheel reports `__version__ == "0.1.0a2"` while declaring 0.1.0a4, so an authorization would record the wrong version of the deciding module. Michael ruled 2026-08-30: a4 remains immutable and identity-verified, and is UNADOPTABLE. Platform CP must pin 0.1.0a5, never 0.1.0a4.

disposition.artifact_identity_evidence: All five proofs, unchanged: the tag peels to 2c61540f74018b7e19d7c5add893e0653cfcdb17; wheel sha256 ad1aaaa2d20b9a565d0656f64762564f4dfd90eb4c367187aa63fdd54a33c37e; sdist sha256 a5dae85d76e17ab34b1868741def46aab514ffba119110ec750794f5dc1c6e2c; a clean read-only consumer installed it with its dependencies; it imported. Independent verify run 33310594187.
disposition.functional_authorization_evidence: service.py:305 `snapshot_digest` returns bare hex; service.py:311 `spec_digest` returns `sha256:`-prefixed; service.py:889 `propose_plan` stores the bare form; service.py:974 `approve_plan` evaluates `evidence.content_digest != row.plan_digest`. A caller supplying the same digest in the other encoding is refused with "the plan changed after approval, so a new approval is required" — a security refusal standing in for a formatting bug.
disposition.version_self_reporting_evidence: __init__.py:172 declares `__version__ = "0.1.0a2"` while pyproject.toml declares 0.1.0a4. Two literals for one fact; nothing compared them because every check read the source tree rather than the built artifact.
disposition.adoption_eligibility_evidence: `pinnable: false`. release_guard.refusals() refuses 0.1.0a4 by NAME, distinctly from the floor, so an attempt to depend on it is a decision someone has to overrule rather than an omission.

releases.release_run_note: THE FIRST RELEASE CUT THROUGH THE CORRECTED TWO-WORKFLOW PATH, and the first verified on SEVEN properties rather than six. Published by run 33318227812 from the exact tip of protected main (b182a99892067f26c0c1d03d958c5fcdc97c5869); that run neither verified itself nor tagged. INDEPENDENT verify run 33318433336 returned VERIFIED: both artifacts fetched from registry.dotmac.io by NAME and sha256-equal to the release build, provenance closed on the peeled commit, publisher read-back, a read-only consumer install WITH the real dependency graph, import, exactly one wheel and one sdist on the index, and — property 7, new here — all seven behavioural canaries passing against the wheel the REGISTRY served rather than against a source checkout. Only that run wrote the tag, on a VERIFIED verdict, through tag_once.py. Supersedes 0.1.0a4, which remains immutable, identity-verified and UNADOPTABLE.
releases.unpinnable_reason: SUPERSEDED BY 0.1.0a6 FOR ITS DECLARED DEPENDENCY FLOOR, NOT FOR ITS ARTIFACT IDENTITY OR ITS BEHAVIOUR. a5's seven verification properties stand and are recorded above unchanged: the bytes on the index are the bytes release run 33318227812 built, and the encoding defect a5 was cut for is genuinely fixed. It is refused here because it cannot be COMPOSED. `service.py:73` reads `from dotmac_kernel.transactions import conflict_savepoint`; `dotmac_kernel/transactions.py` first shipped in dotmac-kernel 0.1.0a98 and is absent from the published 0.1.0a97 wheel, while a5's metadata declares `Requires-Dist: dotmac-kernel (>=0.1.0a77)` — under-constrained by 21 alphas. The Platform CP lane resolved a kernel inside the declared range, wrote a clean lock, matched both published sha256 digests byte-for-byte, and raised ModuleNotFoundError at container boot. Michael ruled 2026-08-30: a5 is immutable and verified, and is UNDER-CONSTRAINED AND UNSUITABLE FOR NEW ADOPTION. Platform CP must pin 0.1.0a6 with dotmac-kernel 0.1.0a98, never 0.1.0a5.

$comment: APPENDED, never a rewrite — the same treatment a4 received, and for a
DIFFERENT failure, which is the point of keeping the two rows side by
side. a4 separated artifact identity from functional behaviour. a5
separates both of those from the DECLARED DEPENDENCY FLOOR: it is the
version whose bytes were right, whose behaviour was right, and whose
metadata described an environment it cannot run in.
This is new evidence, not a record adjusted after the fact. a5's
verification exercised importability in an environment where a
compatible kernel happened to be installed. That proves the wheel
imports; it cannot prove the declared floor is honest, because
nothing in that run ever installed the declared floor.
The tag dotmac-deployment-control-v0.1.0a5 and both artifacts are
never deleted, moved, overwritten or recreated. An index cannot

commits.
disposition.artifact_identity_evidence: All seven properties, unchanged: the tag peels to b182a99892067f26c0c1d03d958c5fcdc97c5869; wheel sha256 c02804b1b9f6dab7becc21696efccdf3820de06dba50903568e2db4c966e0aec; sdist sha256 5883f8ead3caab1a5d93977e6f086ad0f9f2b9df3e5828b5380ea0c41d841ef8; publisher read-back; a read-only consumer installed it with its real dependency graph and imported it; exactly one wheel and one sdist on the index; and all seven behavioural canaries passed against the wheel the registry served. Independent verify run 33318433336.
disposition.functional_authorization_evidence: The defect a5 was cut for is fixed and stays fixed. `PlanDigestV1` makes a digest a value rather than a string, `approve_plan` accepts a4's bare-hex encoding of the plan's own digest, and an unreadable digest raises `DigestEncodingError` rather than claiming the plan changed. Canaries `a4_bare_hex_still_binds` and `encoding_fault_is_not_a_mutation` proved it against the published wheel, and 0.1.0a6 keeps both.
disposition.declared_dependency_floor_evidence: service.py:73 `from dotmac_kernel.transactions import conflict_savepoint`. `dotmac_kernel/transactions.py` is ABSENT from the published dotmac_kernel-0.1.0a97-py3-none-any.whl and PRESENT in dotmac_kernel-0.1.0a98-py3-none-any.whl, both read from registry.dotmac.io. a5's wheel declares `Requires-Dist: dotmac-kernel (>=0.1.0a77)`, so any resolver may satisfy it with a kernel that cannot import the module. Discovered by the Platform CP lane at container boot, after resolution succeeded, the lock wrote cleanly, and both artifacts matched their published hashes exactly.
disposition.adoption_eligibility_evidence: `pinnable: false`. release_guard.refusals() refuses 0.1.0a5 by NAME, distinctly from the floor, so depending on it is a decision somebody has to overrule rather than an omission. 0.1.0a6 declares `>=0.1.0a98` and CI proves that floor in both directions: a lane that installs the declared minimum literally, and a mutation lane that installs the newest kernel the floor excludes and requires the canaries to fail.

releases.release_run_note: THE FIRST RELEASE WHOSE DECLARED DEPENDENCY FLOOR IS ITSELF PROVEN, and the first verified on nine behavioural canaries rather than seven. Published by run 33322980430 from the exact tip of protected main (518711c36e9e5774e11b02c6ab35ec0c9c7b75b9); that run neither verified itself nor tagged. INDEPENDENT verify run 33323067886 returned VERIFIED on all seven properties: both artifacts fetched from registry.dotmac.io by NAME and sha256-equal to the release build, provenance closed on the peeled commit, publisher read-back, a read-only consumer install WITH the real dependency graph, import, exactly one wheel and one sdist on the index, and all NINE behavioural canaries passing against the wheel the REGISTRY served. Only that run wrote the tag, on a VERIFIED verdict, through tag_once.py. WHAT IS NEW HERE AND WAS NOT TRUE OF a5: the wheel declares `Requires-Dist: dotmac-kernel (>=0.1.0a98)`, and that floor is proven in BOTH directions by the required `behavioural canaries (installed wheel)` context on commit 518711c3. The floor lane installed the wheel with dotmac-kernel==0.1.0a98 EXACTLY — the declared minimum, not the resolver's choice — and all nine canaries passed. The mutation lane derived 0.1.0a97 from the index as the newest kernel the floor excludes, observed pip refuse the pairing with `ERROR: Cannot install dotmac-deployment-control==0.1.0a6 and dotmac-kernel==0.1.0a97 because these package versions have conflicting dependencies`, then FORCED a97 in with --no-deps --force-reinstall and observed all nine canaries fail with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'dotmac_kernel.transactions'`. Supersedes 0.1.0a5, which remains immutable, verified on seven properties, and UNDER-CONSTRAINED AND UNSUITABLE FOR NEW ADOPTION.
releases.adoption_note: Adopting a6 obliges a consumer to move from dotmac-kernel a77 to a98 — a 21-alpha jump. Michael's constraint of 2026-08-30: that upgrade receives its own migration and compatibility run and must not be chosen silently by a resolver. Recorded here because the obligation is created by this release and discharged by its consumer.
